entities.name: PMID:25075486
observations: Colombian mixed-species malaria cohort of 862 patients: 533 P. falciparum, 311 P. vivax, and 18 mixed infections.
Low platelet count and high platelet distribution width occurred in 65% each; severe thrombocytopenia below 50,000/µL occurred in 11%.

Patients with complications had lower platelet count and plateletcrit and higher PDW; thrombocytopenia was associated with liver dysfunction and reported alongside severe anemia, neurologic or pulmonary complications, renal impairment, and severe hypoglycemia.
Accessible evidence did not provide numerical effect estimates or species-stratified platelet associations.

entities.name: PMID:33615000
observations: Northwest Colombia cross-sectional study included 50 severe and 56 non-severe P. vivax cases plus 50 healthy controls.
Severe thrombocytopenia occurred in 54% of severe P. vivax cases; hypoglycemia occurred in 48% and liver or kidney failure in 30%.
The study supports a high burden of thrombocytopenia among severe P. vivax cases, but accessible evidence did not quantify an independent platelet-severity effect.

entities.name: Platelet complications Colombia
observations: In Colombian malaria overall, abnormal platelet profiles are associated with clinical complications, based primarily on a mixed-species cohort.
Evidence is insufficient to determine whether the association differs between P. vivax and P. falciparum or whether platelet measures independently predict complications after adjustment.
